clue.text: Elegant conifer

definitions.meaning: smart and neat in dress, as in a trim, well-groomed look
an evergreen cone-bearing tree of the pine family

explanation.definitionFit: One word serves as both an adjective for neat, smart turnout and the name of a common evergreen tree.

clue.text: Corporation grants Tom a choice to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A company gives an employee called Tom some options.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' suggests a company, but it is old jocular slang for a large belly.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporation is humorous dated slang for a pot belly, the belly region.

clue.text: Graduate woman's up for help with addiction

indicators.note: up says the joined pieces are read upwards, which is backwards in a down clue

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate
her is the possessive for a woman

explanation.surface: A female graduate is ready to offer support to addicts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses BAHER in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for rehabilitation, treatment for drug or alcohol dependency.

clue.text: Must society shortly broadcast the state's duties?

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: Soc is the short form of society

explanation.surface: A question whether society must publicise the government's obligations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' scatters MUST and SOC. 'duties' are taxes, not obligations.
explanation.definitionFit: Taxes levied by a government on imported goods are these duties.

clue.text: Fashions Austria rejected abide with the French

indicators.note: rejected says the country's letter is thrown out of the word for abide

parts.note: to abide is to stay
A is the international vehicle code for Austria
les is French for the plural 'the'

explanation.surface: Someone spurns Austrian fashions and sides with the French instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' takes the A out of STAY, leaving STY.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural noun: modes or designs in clothing and hair are its synonyms.

clue.text: Leader of Tories gains a bit of extra time to cover for one of his supporters?

definitions.text: cover for one of his supporters?

indicators.note: leader of takes the opening letter of the word Tories

parts.note: to gain is to win

indicators.note: a bit of takes just the first letter of the word extra

explanation.surface: A Conservative leader is given extra time in office to protect one of his backers.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the stereotype of a twinset and pearls worn by a Conservative-voting woman. Tories are the UK Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A matching jumper and cardigan worn together, a classic British outfit for a woman.

clue.text: Like some missiles left by military agent covering for National Guard?

indicators.note: covering says the defoliant's letters wrap round the two letters for the guard

parts.note: Agent Orange was a herbicide used by the US military in Vietnam
NG is the abbreviation for National Guard

explanation.surface: Weapons left by an army operative standing in for the National Guard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'military agent' suggests a spy, but it is the defoliant Agent Orange, wrapped round NG.
explanation.definitionFit: Missiles designed to strike distant targets are described this way.

clue.text: For starters, swans (upright realistic) reflecting elephants above a lake

definitions.text: For starters, swans (upright realistic) reflecting elephants above a lake

indicators.note: for starters takes the opening letter of each following word, skipping the article

explanation.surface: A description of Dali's painting Swans Reflecting Elephants, with birds on a lake mirrored as elephants.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters of the words (ignoring 'a') spell the answer, and the clue as a whole describes a famous dreamlike painting by Salvador Dali.
explanation.definitionFit: Dali's dreamlike painting of swans whose reflections become elephants is a classic of that bizarre art style.

clue.text: For the Father Deity a temple

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
a deity is a god

explanation.surface: A temple is built to honour God the Father.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiered tower used as a Buddhist or Hindu shrine in East Asia.

clue.text: May possibly, leaving North, see one drawn to the bright lights

definitions.text: one drawn to the bright lights

indicators.note: leaving says the compass letter departs from the word for which May is an example

parts.note: May is one example of a calendar month

explanation.surface: Someone heads south from the north to seek out the glamour of the big city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' removes N from MONTH. The definition reads like a fame-seeker, but it is the insect that flutters round lamps.
explanation.definitionFit: Night-flying insects are famously attracted to lamps and flames.

clue.text: Static from paper etc say

indicators.note: say signals that the word for writing materials is spoken and heard as a different word

parts.note: paper, pens and envelopes together are writing supplies

explanation.surface: A complaint about static electricity coming off paper and similar materials.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words sound alike: one with -ERY for writing supplies, one with -ARY meaning not moving.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective: standing still and not moving, a synonym of static.

clue.text: Supergrass deceived more than half

indicators.note: more than half says only the front six of the ten letters of the synonym are kept

parts.note: to be deceived is to be bamboozled or tricked

explanation.surface: A police informer has been fooled more than half the time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supergrass' looks like a police informer (British slang), but it is a giant grass. Dropping ZLED from BAMBOOZLED leaves six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant woody plant is botanically a member of the grass family, the tallest of them.

clue.text: One of the old school has a computer monitor

parts.note: OB stands for old boy, a former pupil of a school
a server is a computer providing services to a network

explanation.surface: A former pupil owns a computer screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'computer monitor' looks like one item, but 'monitor' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Noun: someone who watches and keeps watch, a synonym for a monitor.

clue.text: Daily aims for distribution to provide it

parts.note: a daily is a cleaning woman, also called a char

indicators.note: for distribution says the letters of aims are dealt out into a new order

explanation.surface: A newspaper plans its distribution so as to deliver some product.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' suggests a newspaper, but it is the British term for a cleaner, a char.
explanation.definitionFit: 'It' is old slang for personal magnetism or allure, the quality of attraction.

clue.text: Ice mostly on rising river and lake

indicators.note: mostly says the synonym loses its final letter

parts.note: ice can mean cold reserve, a chilly aloofness of manner

indicators.note: rising says the word for river reads upwards, backwards in a down clue

parts.note: rio is Spanish and Portuguese for river

explanation.surface: Ice largely covers a river and lake as winter sets in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ice' looks literal but means RESERVE, a cool manner; 'mostly' cuts it to RESERV. 'rising' turns RIO into OIR.
explanation.definitionFit: An artificial body of stored water for supply, like a man-made lake.

clue.text: A wee moose, silly thing, returns

indicators.note: returns says the joined words for moose and silly thing are read backwards

parts.note: the elk is the European name for the moose
a nit is a silly person or fool

explanation.surface: A tiny moose, the silly creature, keeps coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns ELKNIT round. 'A wee' looks like 'a small', but it is a noun: a little urination.
explanation.definitionFit: Noun: childish or informal slang for an act of urinating, a pee.

clue.text: Time to publish paper

parts.note: to issue a book or magazine is to publish it

explanation.surface: It is the moment to bring out a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin soft paper, as in a paper handkerchief or wrapping sheet.

clue.text: Force stateside pooch's declaration of role and nationality

parts.note: a declaration of identity begins 'I'm', a contraction of I am
a pooch is a pet dog
US is the United States, stateside

explanation.surface: An American dog announces its role in the household and its nationality.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as the dog saying "I'm pet, US": its role (pet) and nationality (US).
explanation.definitionFit: Noun: momentum or driving force behind motion or action.

clue.text: Astronomical event-on earth not a special sort

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for earth in electrical wiring

indicators.note: sort means arrange, so the remaining letters are reordered
not says the article's letter is left out of the word special

explanation.surface: An event on Earth unlike any special astronomical happening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' drops the A that the clue names from 'special', and 'sort' then rearranges the six letters left. The hyphen in 'event-on' is just punctuation joining definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: When the Moon passes between Earth and the Sun, blocking sunlight, it is this event.

clue.text: Coat bottom of boat around trace of rust — that's fishy

parts.note: a mac is a raincoat, short for mackintosh

indicators.note: around says the keel's letters are placed round the letter taken from rust

parts.note: the keel is the structure along the bottom of a boat

indicators.note: trace of takes just the opening letter of the word rust

explanation.surface: Someone paints a boat's hull to cover rust, and the job seems suspicious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's fishy' suggests something suspect, but it simply says the answer is a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea fish with striped blue-green skin, so it is indeed a fish.

clue.text: Dainty detective's given latitude

parts.note: Inspector Morse is a fictional Oxford detective from British TV

explanation.surface: A detective is allowed some freedom to investigate.
explanation.walkthrough: Inspector Morse is the detective of a popular British TV series set in Oxford. 'Dainty' is a noun here: a tasty treat.
explanation.definitionFit: Noun: a small delicious bite of food, a delicacy.

clue.text: A fancy sound artist

parts.note: to chime is to ring or sound, like a bell
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Someone takes a liking to a sound artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A fancy' is a noun: an imaginary notion. RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Noun: a wild illusion or fanciful imagining, an impossible dream.

clue.text: Model pie cooked by the book

indicators.note: cooked means altered or prepared, so the letters of pie are reworked

parts.note: a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: A perfect pie made by following the recipe book exactly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges PIE into EPI. 'by the book' reads as 'strictly', but gives TOME.
explanation.definitionFit: A perfect example or embodiment of a quality, an ideal model.

clue.text: Special boat, large, before the Queen's Diamond?

parts.note: an ark is a boat, as in Noah's
L is the abbreviation for large in clothing sizes
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A grand boat leads the Diamond Jubilee pageant on the Thames.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diamond' points to the 2012 Diamond Jubilee river pageant, but 'sparkler' is slang for a diamond.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a gem that glitters, especially a diamond; the question mark marks an informal sense.

clue.text: Strong and unyielding, then stricken to the core — that's rich

parts.note: iron describes a firm, unbending character, as in an iron will

indicators.note: to the core takes the two central letters of the word stricken

explanation.surface: A tough person is deeply shaken, and someone sarcastically remarks on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's rich' is a sarcastic exclamation, matching the answer's sense of meaning the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Exclaiming 'that's rich' points out a mocking contradiction, which is wry and sarcastic in tone.

clue.text: Like an egg, love? Nothing at all?

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
a void is emptiness, nothing at all

explanation.surface: A tennis player wonders if their score of love means nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love' is a tennis score of zero, written as O, which also suits the egg shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective: egg-shaped, from the Latin word for egg.

clue.text: Dodecanese island -head right back to this place for the ambience

indicators.note: head right back says the opening letter of the island goes to the far end

parts.note: Patmos is a Greek island in the Dodecanese group
here means to or at this place

explanation.surface: A traveller heads back from a Greek island to enjoy the mood at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head right back' moves P from the start of PATMOS to the end, giving ATMOSP.
explanation.definitionFit: Noun: the mood or feeling of a place, a synonym of ambience.

clue.text: Instrument essential for tramps

indicators.note: essential means just the core, so the synonym loses its first and last letters

parts.note: hoboes are tramps or vagrants

explanation.surface: A musical instrument is needed by wandering beggars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essential' strips the first and last letters from HOBOES.
explanation.definitionFit: A double-reed woodwind musical instrument used in orchestras.

clue.text: Dock in bay

definitions.meaning: dock is a broad-leaved plant, a relative of a sour herb used in salads
bay is a reddish-brown horse colour, near to a chestnut shade

explanation.definitionFit: One word names both a sour-leaved plant of the dock family and a reddish-brown horse coat colour.

clue.text: He's on course to help bounder stop working

parts.note: a bounder is a cad, a dishonourable man
a machine that dies stops working

explanation.surface: A golfer making steady progress helps out a scoundrel who has quit his job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on course' refers to a golf course. Bounder (CAD) is old British slang for a dishonourable man.
explanation.definitionFit: A golfer's assistant carries clubs around the links and offers advice.
